deep.reconstruction:
PART A (end of the variational-calculus note begun on the previous page). Problem: a Mayer-type problem with a single underdetermined differential side condition f(y',z',y,z,x)=0. The initial point (a1,b1,c1) is fixed. One seeks the curves x -> (y(x),z(x)) satisfying f=0 that reach x=a2, y=b2 with z(a2) minimal. Hilbert treats the minimum value as a function of the end point, Z = Z(x,y) at x=a2, y=b2 (a value function). His plan is to derive the first-order PDE for Z (a Hamilton-Jacobi-type equation) from two derivatives at the end point: (i) along the extremal, and (ii) in the transversal direction.

The transversality relation comes from the first variation. Adjoin the constraint with a multiplier lambda(x). Integrate by parts ('Productintegration'), so the variation is a boundary term plus an integral. On an extremal the Euler-Lagrange equations kill the integral. Setting the boundary term at the upper limit to zero gives, in my reconstruction, lambda[f_{y'}(dy - y'dx) + f_{z'}(dz - z'dx)] = 0 at the end. This is the condition for a surface through the end point on which Z stays minimal when the end point is only required to lie on the surface. The derivative of Z along such a surface is zero, so these surfaces are level sets Z = const, i.e. a transversal field of surfaces. From this the independence theorem (path-independence of Hilbert's invariant integral) is to follow, 'possibly on the basis of my theory of the [diophantine] equation f=0'. This refers to Hilbert's theory of underdetermined (Monge) differential equations, treated by analogy with Diophantine equations, which is the subject of the previous page and of his 1912 Math. Ann. paper.

PART B. Question: when is a definite ternary form f of even degree 2n a sum of 2n-th powers of real linear forms l_i = a_i x + b_i y + c_i z?

Conjecture: probably iff the canonizant ('Kanonisante') is positive. Definition, in symbolic notation f = a_x^{2n}: form a_x^n a_y^n. This is the bilinear form in the degree-n monomials of x and of y. Its symmetric matrix is H[beta,gamma] = c_{beta+gamma}/multinom(beta+gamma), the catalecticant (Hankel/'middle' matrix), with det H the catalecticant/canonizant. det H = 0 is the condition for f to be a sum of fewer 2n-th powers than in general. Example (my addition): for ternary quartics H is 6x6, and det H = 0 iff f is a sum of 5 fourth powers (Clebsch).

Claims: (1) Among definite forms there are just two cases, representable and not. The representable ones can all be deformed continuously into one another (true, since they form a convex cone).
(2) Openness: if f = l_1^{2n} + ... + l_nu^{2n} and det H != 0, every nearby form is also representable. Argument: the representation contains free parameters (one l can be chosen arbitrarily), so there are infinitely many representations. Take mu of them, with mu*nu > dim of the space of 2n-forms. Their mu*nu powers span all 2n-forms, and averaging gives f = sum of all of them (implicit, mine). Then any neighbouring form is sum (1+eps_k) L_k^{2n} with small eps_k, so the coefficients stay positive.
(3) Closedness (next page).
errors: The conjecture as literally stated ('definite and canonizant positive' suffices) is false. Positivity of det H is not the right condition; the necessary condition is H positive semidefinite, since for f = sum l_i^{2n} one has H = sum w_i w_i^T. Counterexample: f = x^2y^2+y^2z^2+z^2x^2+eps(x^4+y^4+z^4) with 0<eps<1/6. It is definite and det H = (eps+1/3)(eps-1/6)^2/216 > 0, yet H has two negative eigenvalues (eps-1/6), so f is not a sum of fourth powers.

Even with 'H positive (semi)definite' the criterion is right only in special cases. For ternary quartics it is right because PSD = SOS there (Hilbert 1888). It fails in general, e.g. for ternary sextics, where H PSD only puts f in the dual of the SOS cone, not in the cone of sums of powers (Reznick 1992).

In the openness argument Hilbert does not show why the extra powers taken from the other representations span the whole space of 2n-forms. Nor does he show how det H != 0 enters. This gap is real: the step needs f in the interior of the cone, which det H != 0 alone does not guarantee in higher degree.

The variational part is a sketch only. The multiplier lambda, the exact transversality formula and the derivation of the PDE are not written out. The appeal to the 'theory of the equation f=0' is unexplained.

results.what: Derivation of the independence theorem for a Mayer problem with Monge side condition via the end-point value function Z and transversal surfaces from the boundary term of the first variation
results.modern_name: Hilbert invariant integral / independence theorem; value function and Hamilton-Jacobi equation; transversality for Mayer problems
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (1900 Paris problems, 23rd; 'Zur Variationsrechnung' Math. Ann. 62, 1906); field theory also Weierstrass, Kneser, Bolza

results.what: Catalecticant (canonizant) of an even form, from a_x^n a_y^n; its vanishing characterizes representation by fewer powers than generic
results.modern_name: catalecticant / middle Hankel matrix; Waring rank

results.what: Conjecture: a definite even ternary form is a sum of even powers of linear forms iff its canonizant is positive
results.modern_name: membership in the cone of sums of 2n-th powers (dual of PSD cone); catalecticant PSD criterion
results.usually_credited_to: Reznick, 'Sums of even powers of real linear forms' (1992); the quartic case follows from Hilbert 1888

results.what: Openness of the set of forms that are positive sums of 2n-th powers near a nondegenerate representation (perturbing positive coefficients over a spanning set of powers)
results.modern_name: interior of the convex cone Q_{3,2n}

deep.surprise_reason: The variational part is Hilbert's known work on the independence theorem. The note on sums of even powers is an unpublished, partly wrong conjecture, but it is interesting. It shows Hilbert linking catalecticant positivity to the cone of sums of powers, which is the theme of Reznick's 1992 memoir, probably close in time to his 1909 Waring identity. The correct version for ternary quartics (H PSD) follows from his own 1888 theorem. That gives it historical interest, but no correct new theorem is stated.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c=symbols('a b c'); x,y,z=symbols('x y z'); w=Matrix([a**2,b**2,c**2,a*b,b*c,c*a]); # catalecticant of (a*x+b*y+c*z)**4 with H[beta,gamma]=coeff(x^(beta+gamma))/multinomial equals w*w.T
checkable.asserts: The catalecticant of a single fourth power is rank-one PSD, so for any sum of fourth powers it is PSD (the necessary condition).
For f=x^2y^2+y^2z^2+z^2x^2+e(x^4+y^4+z^4): det H=(e+1/3)*(e-1/6)**2/216, which is positive for 0<e<1/6.
The eigenvalues are e+1/3 and e-1/6 (double), so H is not PSD for e<1/6 and f is not a sum of 4th powers although det H>0: a counterexample to the literal conjecture.
Ternary quartics form a 15-dimensional space; the catalecticant is 6x6 (indexed by quadratic monomials).
